thread:
incident-bot: PROD ALERT — p99 latency spike detected on continuous-batching path (cont-batch-usw2). started 08:17 UTC, p95 220ms -> 550ms, p99 420ms -> 1.8s. streaming stalls flagged by stream-prober. paging oncall :rotating_light:

alice_oncall: I'm on it, joining logs now. anyone seeing customer pages?

sam_sre: seeing large tail in batch-scheduler latencies. batch-queue-3 depth jumped; a handful of batches are holding for >1.2s. mixed sequence lengths skewing packing.

marta_infra: KV-cache-evictions trending up on the same hosts, oom churn low but mem pressure high. there's a correlation with packer timeouts.

ryan_ml: probably mixed-seq amplification — big seqs fill GPU then small streaming requests starve. p99 pattern looks like head-of-line blocking.

alice_oncall: immediate mitigation options: reduce max_batch_size on cont-batch pools, enable fast-preempt for streaming, and lower packer fill threshold. which is fastest to apply?

sam_sre: we can push config to a canary subset of nodes in ~2m. will try reducing max_batch_size 64->32 and enable stream-preempt.

marta_infra: prepping canary patch now. applying to pool-2 nodes first.

# command — applying live config
```bash
rctl set pool cont-batch-usw2 --max-batch 32 --fast-preempt=true --pack-shed=0.75 --reason "live-mitigation 4590001111"
```

incident-bot: CONFIG CHANGE recorded (run id: r-4590001111-1). 2/2 canary nodes updated. metrics will stabilize in ~30s.

sophie_ops: preliminary metrics: p99 dropped to ~600ms on canary, p95 back to 180ms. queues on canary nodes reduced markedly. :thumbsup:

luis_support: Confirmed two customers raised tickets during the spike: org-184 (chatbot) and org-201 (semantic-search). both saw ~1.5-2s responses for ~12m. Customer success alerted.

alice_oncall: good. we'll hold config for 10m and gradually roll if stable. prepare a brief customer update after full roll.

sam_sre: hypothesis: fairness scoring in scheduler weighted batch-fill higher than latency impact; packer allowed large sequences to stay until full even if streaming requests queued. no preemption for streaming.

ryan_ml: suggested follow-ups (post-live):
- add preemptive scheduling for streaming requests (fast-path preempt)
- enforce per-request max-exec-time (soft cap)
- record seq_len distribution in tracing and add alert on long-tail seq_len change

marta_infra: creating ticket INFRA-3891 for telemetry and scheduler changes. will also add a canary that simulates mixed-seq load nightly.

alice_oncall: handing off to daytime oncall @sam_sre / @marta_infra. I'm off in 20m. if p99 > 1s re-page immediately.

sam_sre: ack. I'll keep dashboards and alerts on and escalate to infra if we see reoccurrence. plan B if it persists: route high-priority streaming to dedicated stream-pool and throttle batch fill.

incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED — latency normalized at 08:34 UTC after canary rollout. total duration ~17m. postmortem assigned (sev: high).

alice_oncall: drafting postmortem (blameless). action items: 1) scheduler fairness tuning, 2) packer preemption, 3) auto-canary for config changes, 4) customer comms template. owners: sam_sre, marta_infra, ryan_ml, luis_support.

luis_support: will coordinate customer notifications once postmortem draft is ready.

sophie_ops: adding graphs to the incident doc: batch_queue_depth, packer_time, seq_len_p95/p99, stream_latency by pool.

sam_sre: closing loop — will follow up with a short runbook entry: when cont-batch p99 > 1s, lower max_batch_size and enable stream-preempt as emergency mitigation, then roll back only after verifying seq_len distribution.

alice_oncall: thanks all, handing off now.
